title: Leek Schnitzel with Israeli Couscous
subtitle: in a sage and white wine butter sauce
description: Steamed leeks coated in breadcrumbs and fried like a schnitzel, served with Israeli couscous in a white wine, sage and butter sauce flavoured with slow-cooked spinach.

steps.text: For the slow-cooked chard, heat 1 tbsp canola oil in a pot, add the chopped chard and cook, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes until it shrinks. Add the rest of the oil and cook over low heat for 3 hours, until the chard turns crisp and black.

Steam the white parts of the leeks for about 45 minutes until soft. Remove and cut a slit lengthways to the centre so they stay joined when opened. Coat in flour, shake off the excess, dip in beaten eggs and roll in breadcrumbs.
Heat oil for deep frying and fry the leek schnitzels for 3 minutes each side until golden. Drain on paper towel.

For the sauce, heat the olive oil in a pot and fry the sliced garlic and sage for about 1 minute until the garlic is lightly golden. Add the wine and cook for about 20 minutes until reduced by half. Add the boiling water, 3 tbsp of the slow-cooked chard and the butter, season with salt and pepper and stir until the butter melts into the sauce. Remove from the heat.
Boil the Israeli couscous in plenty of boiling salted water (1 tbsp salt) for 4 minutes, transfer to iced water and drain.
Add the couscous to the sauce, stir and leave for 5 minutes to absorb the flavours.
Serve the schnitzels with the couscous.
